comparison: Both evaluate viability/safety claims (C28-C31). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with detailed methodological praise. Peer reviewers also SUPPORTED, explicitly noting 'very helpful to see assessment of the viability.' OpenEval additionally includes C52 (citrate synthase activity as safety marker), which peer reviewers address separately in R4.

Both address intensity-dependent EV release (C32-C35, C44). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding data demonstrates clear trends with adequate sample size. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, criticizing the study as 'underpowered' and noting limited exploration of US parameters with only three intensities tested.

Both evaluate Ca²⁺ elevation claims (C36-C38, C40). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding dose-dependent response consistent with EV data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising significant methodological concerns about whole-cell vs. cytosolic Ca²⁺ measurement and potential loss of kinetic information.

Both address Ca²⁺ depletion experiments (C45, C47-C50). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, calling it 'compelling mechanistic evidence.' Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging importance but finding it incomplete—only showing correlation rather than causation, suggesting Ca²⁺ ionophore experiments needed. Peer R4 also includes C52 (safety), which OpenEval addresses in R1.

Both evaluate anti-inflammatory effects in macrophages (C53-C57). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises EV depletion control as critical. Peer reviewers find it 'particularly intriguing' with 'solid data,' though note missing non-inflammatory mRNA control. Strong agreement on this key finding.

Both address concentration-matched experiment (C58, C76-C77). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval calls it 'critical control' distinguishing quantity vs. quality changes. Peer reviewers acknowledge the 'dilution technique' demonstrates number rather than type of vesicles responsible, though note overall mechanistic understanding remains incomplete.

Both evaluate MTT viability data for macrophages (C59). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes it as important control for interpreting gene expression. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of overall positive assessment of viability data throughout study. Complete agreement.

Both address miRNA sequencing data (C66-C75). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding minimal changes important for supporting quantity-over-quality conclusion. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'interpretation of this data fails to draw clear conclusions, diminishing the impact.' Significant disagreement on interpretation value.

Both evaluate mechanistic inference about specific miRNAs (C88). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes claim is 'reasonable but remains speculative' without functional validation. Peer reviewers criticize under general concern about failing to draw clear conclusions from miRNA data. Agreement that claim lacks direct experimental support.

Both address therapeutic/clinical translation claims (C94, C96, C110). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are 'speculative extrapolations' requiring in vivo validation. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly rejecting claims as 'not supported or even addressed by the study.' Peer reviewers more critical, but both agree claims exceed current data.

OpenEval evaluates main study conclusions (C95, C97-C98, C100) as SUPPORTED by collective evidence. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these summary conclusion claims, though peer reviewers' overall assessment acknowledges the study provides solid data on core findings.

OpenEval rates extensive background/literature claims (C1-C26, C39, C41-C43, C46, C60-C65, C78-C87, C89-C93, C101-C104, C106-C109) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual claims, as peer reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than literature review accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates temperature monitoring claim (C105) as SUPPORTED, noting it distinguishes mechanical from thermal effects but actual values not reported. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this methodological control.
